final_answer:
Let
\[
t=1-z,\qquad u=1-G_A(z),\qquad v=1-G_B(z).
\]
Then \(u,v\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), and
\[
G_A-G_B=v-u.
\]

The generating-function equations are
\[
G_A=z\left(\frac12+\frac38G_A^2+\frac18G_B^2\right),
\]
\[
G_B=z\left(\frac12+\frac14G_A+\frac14G_B^3\right).
\]

Define
\[
s=\frac{u+v}{2},\qquad \delta=v-u=G_A-G_B.
\]
Thus
\[
u=s-\frac{\delta}{2},\qquad v=s+\frac{\delta}{2}.
\]

Expanding the two equations in \(u,v,t\), we obtain
\[
u=t+\frac34u+\frac14v-t\left(\frac34u+\frac14v\right)
-\frac38u^2-\frac18v^2+O(tu^2),
\]
and
\[
v=t+\frac14u+\frac34v-t\left(\frac14u+\frac34v\right)
-\frac34v^2+\frac14v^3+O(tv^2).
\]

Adding and subtracting these equations gives, to the orders needed,
\[
0=2t-2ts-\frac54s^2-\frac12s\delta+\frac14s^3+O(t^2),
\tag{1}
\]
and
\[
\frac{\delta}{2}
=-\frac14s^2-s\delta+\frac14s^3+O(t^2).
\tag{2}
\]

Since \(s=O(t^{1/2})\) and \(\delta=O(t)\), write
\[
s=\kappa t^{1/2}+a t+O(t^{3/2}).
\]

From (2), using \(\delta=-\frac12s^2+O(t^{3/2})\),
\[
\delta=-\frac12s^2+\frac32s^3+O(t^2).
\tag{3}
\]

Now substitute the expansion for \(s\) into (1). The coefficient of \(t\) gives
\[
2-\frac54\kappa^2=0,
\]
so
\[
\kappa^2=\frac85,\qquad \kappa=\sqrt{\frac85}.
\]

The coefficient of \(t^{3/2}\) in (1) gives
\[
-2\kappa-\frac52\kappa a+\frac12\kappa^3=0,
\]
hence
\[
a=-\frac{12}{25}.
\]

Finally, substituting \(s=\kappa t^{1/2}+at+O(t^{3/2})\) into (3),
\[
\delta
=-\frac{\kappa^2}{2}t
+\left(-\kappa a+\frac32\kappa^3\right)t^{3/2}
+o(t^{3/2}).
\]
Therefore
\[
\alpha=\frac{\kappa^2}{2}=\frac45,
\]
and
\[
\beta=-\kappa a+\frac32\kappa^3
=\frac{72}{25}\kappa
=\frac{72}{25}\sqrt{\frac85}.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{\left(\kappa,\alpha,\beta\right)
=
\left(\sqrt{\frac85},\ \frac45,\ \frac{72}{25}\sqrt{\frac85}\right)}.
\]
